title: An AI-guided TESS search flagged a planet candidate around G 249-11
summary: An agent-guided search of archived TESS observations found repeating dips around the nearby red dwarf G 249-11 at a period of about 5.31 days. An ephemeris fitted to two sectors predicted dips in two held-out sectors. If the signal comes from a planet, its fitted radius is about 1.6 times Earth’s.
ai_technology: Claude Sonnet 5.5; Infinity Machine research agent

source_review.scope: Zenodo v1 author research note record; Infinity Machine §3.6 and Appendix A.10 source and held-out test

evidence.tested: The author used two sectors for initial fitting and two other existing sectors for a timing check. A combined false-alarm probability of about 0.002 was estimated from 400 end-to-end null realizations.
evidence.unknown: A bound eclipsing companion and a nearby faint source remain plausible alternatives. The candidate is unconfirmed; the held-out data came from existing observations.
evidence.ai_role: Claude Sonnet 5.5 proposed and executed a box-least-squares search of TESS light curves. The author applied photometric, catalogue and held-out timing checks.
